bioMérieux S.A. (BIM.PA) stock price, news, quote and history
sum: bioMérieux S.A. develops, manufactures, and markets in vitro diagnostic solutions for infectious diseases in France, Europe, Africa, the Middle East, North and South America, the Asia Pacific, and internationally. It operates through Clinical Applications and Industrial Applications segments. The company offers CHROMID RANGE, a chromogen culture media; air, surface, and water monitoring systems; BACT/ALERT VIRTUO, a blood sample culture system; BIOFIRE, a multiplex polymerase chain reaction system (PCR); BIOFIRE SPOTFIRE, a lowplex PCR point-of-care system; VITEK MS, a mass spectrometry system; VITEK 2, an automated identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) system; API RANGE standardized ID strips; VITEK REVEAL, a rapid AST system; ETEST, a gradient method on culture media; BIOMERIEUX EPISEQ CS, a whole genome sequencing solution for epidemiologic monitoring; VIDAS, a specific marker of severe bacterial infections/sepsis; and Biomérieux vision suite, a software that provides information to support diagnosis and clinical decision making. It also provides culture media and associated instruments; ARGENE that provides PCR tests for diagnosing viral respiratory diseases; EMAG system and NUCLISENS extraction reagents for DNA and RNA extraction; GENE-UP and VERIFLOW for detection of microorganisms for the food industry; ETEST for manual measurement of minimum inhibitory concentration of an antibiotic; API and RAPIDEC CARBA NP for identification of bacteria and manual antimicrobial susceptibility testing; BIOBALL for quantitative microbiological quality control; CHEMUNEX, a microbiology instrument; ENDONEXT for detection of endotoxins; TEMPO for fluorescence counting of bacteria; and Hybiome, a CLIA technology, as well as lab consultancy service and training modules. The company was formerly known as B-D Mérieux. The company was founded in 1963 and is headquartered in Marcy-l'Étoile, France. bioMérieux S.A. operates as a subsidiary of Institut Mérieux SA.

Korea National Railway discusses AI drawing comparison and BIM clash checks; KCC E&C earns top honors
sum: At the Railway Construction BIM Competition and Railway Smart, BIM and AI Technology Forum, held on the 11th at Korea National Railway’s headquarters in Daejeon, Chairman Jeong Jin-hyeok delivers opening remarks. Photo courtesy of Korea National Railway [Financial News] Korea National Railway shared examples of improvements to work at railway construction sites using building information modeling (BIM) and artificial intelligence (AI). Participants discussed ways to expand the use at construction sites of technologies such as checking for clashes between structures in advance and automatically comparing design drawings with 3D models.
Korea National Railway said it had held the Railway Construction BIM Competition and Smart, BIM and AI Technology Forum jointly with the Korea BIM Society at its headquarters in Daejeon on the 11th.
BIM is a technology that represents the shape of structures and related information in 3D digital models for use in design, construction and maintenance.

Twenty construction sites took part in the Railway Construction BIM Competition. After a review of written submissions, three construction sections with outstanding results in improving work practices received awards from the chairman of Korea National Railway.

The top prize went to KCC E&C, which is responsible for Section 5 of the Gangneung–Jejin Railway Construction Project. The company was recognized for improving on-site work by developing a BIM-based model to check for structural clashes in advance.

At the technology forum, five of the 12 applicant organizations selected received Korea BIM Society Technology Awards and presented their results. Hanul C&B received the highest evaluation for its quality-review technology for design deliverables, which uses AI to automatically compare design drawings with BIM models.
The panel discussion addressed challenges and future directions for applying smart, BIM and AI technologies at construction sites, as well as ways to cooperate to expand their use.

Archinect Meets: Andrés Rincón Caballero of World Architecture Inspiration
sum: In today's episode of Archinect Meets, we connect with Andrés Rincón Caballero, founder of the popular World Architecture Inspiration social media channels.

A trained architect and BIM expert, Caballero employs his professional background to enrich his educational storytelling about iconic buildings, noteworthy architects, fascinating city planning, and history-making style periods.

Our conversation also touches on the pitfalls of building an online presence: A cyberattack on the World Architecture Inspiration Instagram account this summer wiped out an audience of more than 640,000 followers he had built over three years, prompting him to recreate the popular channel from scratch. "We’re starting again," Caballero defiantly shared in his inaugural post on the new WAI account in July. "And we’ll build it stronger than ever."

I started World Architecture Inspiration in 2023 because, while working as a BIM manager, I was feeling increasingly detached from architecture. I wanted to reconnect with the passion that had led me to study it in the first place. That was the spark behind WAI.

I had no experience filming, speaking to an audience, or editing videos. I had to learn everything on my own, without AI to help me along the way. I started simply by reposting projects I liked as carousels. Then I began telling stories about those projects and eventually sharing my own projects as well. It was a gradual process of teaching myself how to communicate what I found interesting about architecture.

Today, WAI is evolving into an architecture media platform, while I’m also developing separate projects involving design and personal brands. What started as a way to reconnect with my passion has opened up different ways for me to practice, explore, and communicate architecture.
I’d say roughly 40% comes from my own interests and curiosity, and the rest is shaped by audience feedback, performance, and trending topics.

BIM Group partners with IRONMAN: From the Hawai'i model to the Phu Quoc aspiration.
sum: The story of the IRONMAN race's development in Hawai'i is a classic example of how sporting events can be linked to tourism and leisure, enhancing the appeal of a coastal and island destination. In partnership with this global sporting event brand, BIM Group strives to make Phu Quoc one of the world's leading tourist destinations, where the journey of conquest is extended by experiences beyond the race track.

The Hawai'i Islands are the birthplace of IRONMAN, with the first race held on Oʻahu in 1978. In 1981, for traffic safety reasons, the race moved to Kailua-Kona, on the west side of the Big Island. Here, the lava fields lining the route became the iconic backdrop for the endurance challenge, becoming an integral part of the race's image for decades.

For athletes, Kona - Hawai'i is associated with the aspiration to conquer the highest peaks. Through images of the competition, the landscapes of Hawai'i also reach the global sports community. This connection shows how an international event can add depth to the destination experience: the competition journey opens up opportunities to explore nature, relax, and spend time with loved ones.

This is also the direction that BIM Group is pursuing in Phu Quoc, partnering with Sunrise Events Vietnam to bring IRONMAN series races to the island since 2022. Built on the foundation of the resort development at Phu Quoc Marina, sporting events create another reason for tourists to choose Phu Quoc and experience the island.

When Mark Allen, a six-time IRONMAN World Championship winner, visited Phu Quoc as an inspirational ambassador in 2024, he recognized the similarities between the island and Kona. He encouraged athletes to share their experiences with the race and the organization in Phu Quoc with their communities.

While the Kona race track evokes the atmosphere of lava fields, Phu Quoc offers a racing experience set against a tropical backdrop, with long stretches of sand and turquoise waters at Bai Truong Beach. The landscape contributes to the race's unique character, while also providing opportunities for relaxation and recreation for athletes and their families.
Kailua-Kona and Bai Truong also share similarities in location, both situated on the western side of the island and close to the airport.

items.t: GSBIM turns laser scans into photorealistic building models with centimetre-level textures
sum: Building Information Models have become the standard digital backbone of construction and facility management, yet most as-built BIM reconstructions still look disappointingly plain. According to a new study published in Multimedia Tools and Applications, models rebuilt from real-world scans typically appear as bare geometric surfaces or rely on artificially assigned textures, an absence of real-world appearance that limits visual interpretability, reduces immersion in digital environments and restricts downstream tasks that depend on surface texture, such as defect detection and facility inspection. The paper, authored by Yuyang Jin, Siyi Li, Lihui Huang, Nanying Liang and Yiyu Cai, introduces a framework called GSBIM that fuses laser-scanned point clouds, industry-standard BIM geometry and a rapidly maturing 3D rendering technique known as Gaussian Splatting into a single photorealistic, metrically consistent model.

The core problem the researchers identify is one of disconnected pipelines. Existing image-to-BIM texture mapping methods often depend on image feature registration or manual alignment and can be affected by occlusions, the authors write. Meanwhile, Gaussian Splatting provides photorealistic view synthesis, but standard image-driven pipelines usually rely on Structure-from-Motion and produce standalone Gaussian representations that are not inherently constrained to the shared LiDAR and BIM metric frame. In other words, the visually striking renders produced by Gaussian Splatting have historically lived in their own coordinate universe, detached from the precisely measured BIM geometry that engineers and facility managers actually use. GSBIM addresses this by integrating IFC-based as-built BIM, point-cloud-derived IFC texture maps and geometry-constrained LiDAR Gaussian Splatting in a shared coordinate system, so that rendered output is anchored to the same metric frame as the underlying building model.

A key innovation lies in how the framework acquires its training views. Perspective training views and camera poses are derived from registered scanner panoramas and scan poses, avoiding manual alignment between images, point clouds and BIM geometry.

Why BIM Still Doesn't Know What Your Building Is Made Of
sum: Move a wall in Revit and every plan, section and schedule follows. Change a material, though, and the team is often back in specifications, spreadsheets and drawings, checking that they all describe the same choice.

For Dave Lemont, who led Revit Technology before Autodesk acquired it, that gap is BIM's unfinished work. Now Executive Chairman of Acelab, he is focused on a Material Intelligence Model: one structured product record, connected to every document where that selection appears. It is also something architects can now try for themselves, since Acelab has opened Material Hub search to anyone, no account required.
In this conversation, he discusses what connected material data means for architects and owners, where AI helps, and why the final call still belongs to the designer.
Eduardo Souza (ArchDaily): When you were bringing Revit to market, what did you hope to change about architectural practice?
Dave Lemont (Acelab): Everything was 2D. The plan, section, elevation and schedule were drawn separately, as unrelated drawings that happened to describe the same building. Move a

wall and someone had to find it again in each one and change it by hand. The breakthrough was the parametric building model: one model, with every drawing as a view of it. Change the model and the drawings update; edit a drawing and the model updates. The name Revit came from "revise instantly." The larger idea, which later took the name BIM, was that a building could be represented as intelligent objects carrying all the material information, not just geometry.
AD: Why is material information still so difficult to connect across tools and documents?

Why construction firms can’t afford outdated IT systems
sum: Construction may happen on site, but much of the work that keeps a project moving now happens digitally. Your team checks drawings on tablets, shares documents through the cloud, prices jobs using specialist software and communicates with subcontractors across multiple locations. Technology is also instrumental in the planning phase, with tools like 3D modelling and GPS mapping. As that reliance grows, ageing IT is more than an inconvenience. It can influence everything from your ability to win new business to how your projects run.

Outdated technology costs you in small increments – of money, of errors, of time – that eventually add up. Customers, clients and staff will become frustrated by long loading times, manual data entry and analysis, information errors, scattered files and outdated software and machinery that impact how effectively your company is able to perform.

Inefficient systems can also risk your ability to compete for new business. If you’re getting negative reviews relating to your speed, accuracy and responsiveness, customers are likely to go elsewhere. The most successful construction businesses aren’t simply reactive to the rapid progression of technology – they build IT into the core of the business plan.

Construction firms hold information that criminals can exploit, and it’s vital you build strong foundations against online threats to keep this data safe. Under the Data Protection Act 2018 and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you’re legally required to safeguard personal customer data. Your data, such as commercial documents, staff details, payment information and project plans, also requires protection from theft and fraud.

Older systems become particularly problematic when vendors stop supporting them, because your business may no longer receive the updates needed to address newly discovered vulnerabilities. The NCSC warns that construction businesses face threats including spear-phishing, ransomware and supply-chain attacks.

Identify unsupported operating systems and applications and apply available security updates or arrange replacements where necessary, according to risk. Even with new systems, strong cybersecurity relies on everyday controls.

items.t: Stefanutti Stocks : Re-Engineering Africa’s Built Environment
sum: Stefanutti Stocks is reshaping Southern Africa’s construction landscape through multidisciplinary expertise, digital innovation, and sustainable infrastructure solutions. Russell Crawford, CEO, tells us how the group continues to navigate challenges whilst building for future growth.

The construction industry in South Africa (SA) has evolved alongside the country’s built environment and urban growth, demonstrating resilience through successive periods of economic, social, and technological change.
Since the 19th century, the construction industry has had a profound impact on SA’s socioeconomic makeup, driven by the changing needs of the nation’s infrastructure and rapid technological change.
Construction has been closely linked to SA’s mining sector for more than a century, supporting industrialisation, urbanisation, labour mobility, and infrastructure development since the late 1800s.

Indeed, the growing mining industry at the time generated greater demand for critical infrastructure such as railways and bridges, logistics and transport, industrial buildings, roads, and evolving urban settlements.

The expansion and diversification of the construction industry was therefore not an isolated event, as it evolved in the early 1900s from local building activity into an increasingly multidisciplinary landscape concerning labour movement, transport, materials, and urbanisation.

The discovery of gold on the Witwatersrand in 1886 led directly to the founding of Johannesburg, which within a decade had become the country’s largest town. Into the 20th century, deep-level mining and a growing manufacturing base drove sustained investment in transport, industrial, and urban infrastructure.

HDAC1/2 maintain alveolar macrophage homeostasis through Bim and LSD1
sum: A study led by Professor Li Wu at the Institute of Immunology, Tsinghua University, was published in Volume 2 of the journal Immunity & Inflammation on October 19, 2026. The article reports that HDAC1 and HDAC2 are key epigenetic regulators of alveolar macrophages (AMs), jointly promoting their differentiation and survival. Combined deletion of HDAC1 and HDAC2 leads to severe AM loss, alveolar proteinosis-like pathological changes, and significantly increased susceptibility to influenza virus infection in mice.

AMs are among the most important tissue-resident macrophages in the lung. They serve as the first line of immune defense against respiratory pathogens and are essential for maintaining the metabolism of pulmonary surfactant and lung homeostasis. Multiple cytokines and transcription factors have been identified as regulators of AM development and differentiation; however, the role of epigenetic regulation in maintaining AM homeostasis has remained to be further clarified.

HDAC1 and HDAC2 belong to class I histone deacetylases. They share high sequence similarity and exhibit functional redundancy in many cell types. In this study, the researchers found that combined deletion of Hdac1 and Hdac2 led to near-complete loss of AMs, whereas deletion of Hdac1 or Hdac2 alone had no obvious effect on AM numbers. Using different Cre-driven conditional gene knockout systems and competitive bone marrow chimeric experiments, the team confirmed that HDAC1 and HDAC2 exert important cell-intrinsic regulatory effects on AM maintenance.

The study further showed that HDAC1/2 deficiency produces pathological consequences beyond macrophage loss. AMs not only maintain the alveolar environment but also form an important component of respiratory innate immune defense. Mice with combined HDAC1/2 deficiency displayed obvious alveolar proteinosis-like features, including significantly elevated total protein levels in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and accumulation of surfactant proteins in lung tissue.

sum: Electromech Infraprojects files DRHP for IPO with fresh issue of up to ₹326 crore

Electromech Infraprojects Ltd on Monday (October 26) said it has filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) for an initial public offering (IPO) comprising a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹326 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 18,91,000 equity shares by existing shareholders.
The DRHP, dated September 23, 2026, marks a step towards the company's proposed listing in the capital markets. The equity shares will have a face value of ₹5 each.

Electromech Infraprojects provides mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) solutions across data centres, Global Capability Centres (GCCs), and commercial and industrial projects. Its capabilities cover technical design, engineering, procurement, project execution, testing and commissioning.

The company's execution model integrates procurement, engineering and quality control, supported by project-management systems such as Building Information Modelling (BIM). The technology enables integrated three-dimensional modelling of its MEP scope to identify and resolve design clashes before site work begins.

As of March 31, 2026, the company had an order book of ₹829.72 crore across 45 ongoing projects. Data centres accounted for ₹729.46 crore (87.92%), GCCs for ₹37.36 crore (4.50%) and commercial and industrial projects for ₹62.90 crore (7.58%). The DRHP also identifies a 48 MW data-centre project in Telangana, with an order book value of ₹501 crore, exclusive of GST, as one of its larger ongoing assignments.
The contribution of repeat customers to revenue from operations increased from 87% in fiscal 2024 to 89% in fiscal 2025 and 95% in fiscal 2026, according to the DRHP.

Telge Projects Ltd is engaged in a comprehensive range of engineering design services, and company information says it was incorporated on 16 January 2018. It is an engineering design and BIM services provider for EPC firms, fabricators and contractors, offering 3D modelling, structural engineering design, material take-offs, 2D drafting and architectural design with a focus on BIM-driven 3D workflows. sum: SpyGlass Pharma Announces Positive 4-Year Data From First-in-Human Trial of Its Innovative BIM-IOL System
Four-year interim data cover 21 evaluable patients, with 18 remaining off all topical eye-pressure-lowering drops.

Rhea-AI Sentiment reads the wording of the document, how positive or negative its language is on a 1 to 5 scale. The balance of points shown with the takes weighs what the document actually discloses, so the two can disagree, for example when a trial that missed its main goal is described in upbeat language.
SpyGlass Pharma (SGP) announced four-year interim results from its first-in-human trial of the Bimatoprost Drug Pad-IOL System, or BIM-IOL System.

The trial involves patients with mild-to-moderate open angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension undergoing routine cataract surgery. Among 21 evaluable patients, mean intraocular pressure, the pressure inside the eye, fell 37% across all three dose groups, from 25.1 ± 2.5 mmHg at baseline after washout to 15.9 ± 2.8 mmHg. At four years, 86% (18 of 21) remained off all topical pressure-lowering drops, and 90% maintained best corrected distance visual acuity of at least 20/25. No product-related adverse events were reported.
The trial was designed to evaluate safety and efficacy over seven years; the company plans to follow patients through 2029.
- Moderate pointMean eye pressure fell 37% across all three dose groups at four years versus baseline after washout.

Autodesk’s most ambitious AI play yet
sum: At Autodesk University Autodesk presented an AI ambition that goes beyond faster tools: a connected Assistant that decides how to solve tasks on your behalf. But as Greg Corke found on the Expo floor, there’s also a growing appetite for local AI, keeping data and costs firmly under control

Autodesk no longer just wants to sell you better software; it wants to do a lot of your work for you. At Autodesk University 2026, that ambition was presented as ‘Project Intelligence’, described by Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost during his keynote as a “connected brain at the centre that brings every data point, every decision, every discipline together – a brain that grows smarter as a project advances.”

Naturally, AI dominated the agenda. Almost every major announcement came wrapped in talk of agents, models and context. What set this AU apart from the previous two, however, was a shift from talk of time-saving features in individual CAD and BIM tools to a more ambitious AI proposition: an intelligent AI intended to turn a user’s stated intent into work they can review, refine, and use, without them having to navigate products, workflows, data and complex UIs. In other words, users state what they want, and Autodesk becomes the orchestrator calling on the relevant tools from its broad software ecosystem.
The headline announcement was that Autodesk Assistant is going solo. Anagnost explained that it will be available as a “standalone agent-first experience, one that reaches across products.”

Mike Haley, SVP research gave the rationale in the pre-event press briefing stating that it is “for work that doesn’t fit neatly inside a product like Revit or AutoCAD or Fusion.” The software is still in development and expected to launch next year.
Discover what’s new in technology for architecture, engineering and construction — read the latest edition of AEC Magazine

Standalone Assistant is not a replacement for the Assistants already found inside Revit, AutoCAD, Fusion, Civil 3D, Forma Data Management, Autodesk Build and others. In fact, Amy Bunszel, executive VP, AEC solutions, confirmed that Autodesk will keep expanding the in-product versions.

Digital Twin Market Size, Global Report | 2035 MRFR
sum: The Digital Twin Market was valued at USD 39.45 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 53.60 billion in 2026 before climbing to USD 1,085.20 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 38.70% during the 2026–2035 forecast window. This acceleration is anchored in two converging forces: widespread industrial IoT platform maturation and a wave of government mandates requiring a real-time digital twin for energy grid management across safety-critical infrastructure in the US, EU, and China. The US Department of Energy's 2024 allocation of USD 1.2 billion toward grid modernization programs specifically earmarked digital-replica capabilities for transmission monitoring .

Physics-informed, cloud-native simulation environments combining sensor data, AI inference and 3D visualization replace legacy siloed SCADA and CAD-based design procedures. Global spending on enterprise IoT-based digital twin for smart manufacturing surpassed USD 8 billion in 2024, led by automotive OEMs and semiconductor fabs seeking 12–18% yield gains through virtual process optimization [3]. Industrial digital twin for predictive maintenance already underlies more than 40% of new condition monitoring contracts signed by Tier-1 equipment vendors .

North America holds over 41.0% of the Digital Twin Market, driven by defense-sector digital-thread programs and hyperscaler cloud spending. Asia-Pacific is the fastest expanding area at an expected 28.10% CAGR, fueled by China’s “Digital China 2035” vision and India’s Smart Cities Mission. Europe has the second-highest share at around 26.5%, with Germany and France leading the way in adoption in the automotive and aerospace sectors. The Digital Twin Market will change the way enterprises develop, run and decommission physical assets of all sizes during the next decade.
- Manufacturing accounted for 37.90% of the Digital Twin Market share in 2025, reflecting entrenched smart-factory deployments across automotive, electronics, and heavy industry
- Oil & Gas is forecast to expand at a 30.20% CAGR through 2035, as producers adopt asset-integrity digital twins to reduce unplanned downtime in offshore and refinery operations

items.t: Bim Pepple leads the way but Plymouth Argyle are spreading goals around
sum: Argyle have scored 14 goals in league and cup this season and they have come from nine different players
Tom Cleverley believes Plymouth Argyle are making it difficult for other teams to defend against them because they can score goals in a variety of different ways.
The Pilgrims have netted 14 times this season - with 10 goals in six League One games, plus four more in a couple of Carabao Cup matches.

Those goals have been shared among nine players, with Bim Pepple leading the way on three after he was on target with Argyle's third goal in their 3-0 league win against Barnsley at Home Park on Saturday.

Xavier Amaechi, Will Evans and Oli Irow, the loan signing from Tottenham Hotspur, have all scored twice, while there has been one goal apiece for Ronan Curtis, Alex Hartridge, Julio Pleguezuelo, Caleb Watts and Harvey White.

Cleverley said: "It's really good we are a team that has different avenues of scoring. Set plays is an avenue, direct football like you saw from the kick-off (against Barnsley) is an avenue, controlled possession in their half is an avenue.

"Then quality and combinations like you saw at Wycombe is a different avenue. We are a hard team to prepare against to defend and that's because we have a spread of personnel who can score the goals and a spread of avenues to get them."

sum: The initiative involved preparing and serving meals at social institutions in Tete and Zambézia, as well as distributing food hampers to elderly people in Cabo Delgado, benefiting approximately 860 people, including children, older persons and other individuals in situations of greater social vulnerability.

In Tete, the activity took place at the Rainha da Paz Reception Centre. In Zambézia, the initiative was carried out at the Sinacura Open Centre. In Cabo Delgado, food hampers were distributed to elderly beneficiaries previously identified by Millennium bim’s local teams.

More than providing material assistance, the “Solidarity Soup” initiative sought to create meaningful moments of connection and sharing between the Bank’s employees and the beneficiary communities, promoting the values of solidarity, social inclusion and active citizenship.

According to Rui Pedro, Chairman of the Executive Committee of Millennium bim, “Volunteering is an integral part of Millennium bim’s culture and of the way our employees engage with the communities where they live and work. The ‘Solidarity Soup’ initiative is a clear example of their willingness to dedicate their time, energy and care to those who need it most, creating moments of sharing and human connection that go far beyond material support.”

The initiative relied on the voluntary participation of Millennium bim employees, who dedicated their time to this solidarity action, helping deliver support and meaningful moments of connection to hundreds of beneficiaries across the three provinces.
Through this initiative, Millennium bim combined corporate volunteering with direct social support, strengthening the relationship between its employees and the beneficiary communities.

items.t: Millennium BIM Mozambique posts profit of 201 million meticais in 2025
sum: Profits at Millennium BIM Mozambique, part of Portugal’s Millennium BCP, fell sharply in 2025 to 201 million meticais (€2.7 million), impacted by the bank’s exposure to public debt, according to its annual report and accounts.

The bank pointed in particular to the effects of the downgrade of Mozambique’s sovereign debt rating, which led to “the recognition of additional impairments associated with public debt, with relevant impacts on the evolution of the bank’s results”.

The management of Millennium BIM — one of Mozambique’s two systemic banks, with almost 2.3 million clients — states in the report that it had to set aside 5.9 billion meticais (€79.5 million) in impairments related to Mozambican public debt. In 2024, the bank had reported profits of 3.309 billion meticais (€44.6 million).

The sharp fall in 2025 profits, following a 54% decline in 2024 compared with the 2023 net result, when profits reached 7.211 billion meticais (€97.2 million), was also attributed to an increase in credit impairment resulting from a greater probability of default by certain customer segments, influenced by both the adverse macroeconomic context and the reassessment of internal risk models.
The bank decided to allocate 2025 profits to free and legal reserves, with no dividend distribution, as was also the case in 2024.

Millennium BIM’s banking income rose 6.5% in 2025 to 19.229 billion meticais (€259.2 million), while total assets fell 0.53% to 200.877 billion meticais (€2.708 billion). Net loans to customers increased 9.14% to 49.288 billion meticais (€664 million), while customer deposits grew 2.65% to 160.935 billion meticais (€2.169 billion). Equity remained virtually unchanged at 34.632 billion meticais (€467 million).

According to the report and accounts, 2.68% of the bank’s total loan portfolio was non-performing in December, down from 2.92% a year earlier, 3.08% in 2023 and 7.85% in 2022. However, overdue loans of more than 90 days covered by impairments rose from 144.66% to 275.28% over the past year.

items.t: Korea Shares Expressway Expertise with Peru
sum: 15 Peruvian Officials Begin Road Operations Training on May 17

The Korea Expressway Corporation will conduct a training program on “Enhancing Capacity for Road Operation and Maintenance” for 15 officials from Peru’s Ministry of Transport and Communications at the KOICA Training Center from on May 17 through 30. The program was prepared as part of the Korea International Cooperation Agency’s (KOICA) global training program, and since 2024 it has invited Peruvian policy practitioners each year to spread Korea’s advanced road technologies.

This year’s training course is notable for having been substantially revamped in line with the government’s policy drive to expand AI infrastructure exports. The curriculum includes Korea’s road traffic policies, smart construction technologies based on AI and BIM, and AI application technologies for expressways. Trainees will also visit advanced transport infrastructure sites, including the Smart Construction Integrated Control Center and the K-City research complex, to see Korea’s technological capabilities firsthand.

A special session will also be held to support the overseas expansion of outstanding domestic small and medium-sized enterprises. Participating companies are set to introduce their proprietary smart road management technologies to the Peruvian side, including an AI warning system for slopes, pavement detection systems, and overloaded vehicle enforcement systems.

The Korea Expressway Corporation previously carried out the “Smart Road Management Master Plan” project in on July 2024 to introduce traffic management technology to Peru’s major arterial roads. In on June 2026, it plans to pursue the “Feasibility Study for the Establishment of Smart ITS on the Lima-Chancay Section in Peru” project.

A Korea Expressway Corporation official said, “We believe Korea’s expressway operation experience and technological capabilities will make a substantial contribution to raising the level of Peru’s road infrastructure,” adding, “We hope this training will strengthen cooperation with Central and South American countries and serve as an opportunity for domestic companies to take a leap forward in the field of AI-based digital road management.”

Ucross to Host Farewell Happy Hour for Bim Eriksson
sum: On May, 15, 2026, Ucross Foundation, the acclaimed artist residency program in northern Wyoming, announced that they will host a farewell happy hour honoring Bim Eriksson of Stockholm, Sweden, an artist-in-residence at Ucross through the European Union Delegation to the United States, on Wednesday, May 27, from 4 to 6 pm., at The Warehouse Gastropub in Sheridan.

A visual artist and storyteller from Stockholm, Eriksson has spent her residency connecting with the local community while developing new creative projects as part of the EU’s Transatlantic Rising Stars initiative, which fosters artistic exchange and collaboration between European and American artists.

Working across comics, drawing and multidisciplinary storytelling, Eriksson’s practice explores emotional complexity, identity, power structures and soft resistance, often balancing the playful with the unsettling. During her residency, she collaborated with Sheridan artist Polly Burge and Buffalo poet David Romtvedt , a Ucross alumnus.
Eriksson also presented a community artist talk at Sheridan College on April 30.

Eriksson will have an open studio during Ucross Founder’s Day on May 30. She will then travel to Washington, D.C. following her residency at Ucross, where she, Burge and Romtvedt will present their collaborative works at a special event hosted at the Hirshhorn Museum, in Washington, D.C. presented by the European Union Delegation to the United States, in June.

“It has been a joy to see how Bim has connected with our neighboring communities in Sheridan and Buffalo, as well as her fellow artists-in-residence, over her eight -week residency,” said Caitlin Addlesperger , President and Executive Director of Ucross. “We invite you to come say hello to Bim, discover her artwork and enjoy a taste of Sweden.”

During the farewell happy hour, guests are invited to gather on The Warehouse Gastropub patio for a preview of Eriksson’s projects with Burge and Romtvedt, as well as her solo work. The Warehouse Gastropub will provide a smorgasbord of Swedish-inspired bites curated by Head Chef Jeff Armstrong and Owner Christer Johansson , originally of Trollhättan, Sweden. The evening will feature an artist talk by Eriksson, as she concludes her time in Wyoming.

items.t: Wizz: Interview With CEO Thomas Donninger About The Social Networking App Company
sum: Wizz is a social networking/messaging app mainly aimed at Gen Z and young adults. The app helps users meet new people and make friends online. Pulse 2.0 interviewed Wizz CEO Thomas Donninger to learn more.
Could you tell me more about your background? Donninger said:
“I’m the CEO of Wizz, a Gen Z–focused social discovery app. I’ve been building mobile products for over 10 years.”

“I studied computer science at Epitech and started my career at a traditional IT consulting firm. I quickly realized I didn’t want to execute other people’s roadmaps, I wanted to build my own products.”

“ Less than a year later, I launched my first company, Vili&Ve, a design and product studio that partnered with early-stage startups and first-time founders to help them shape their visual identity, from marketing websites to the look and feel of their actual products. We worked with fast-growing French startups like Dreem (formerly Rythm) and Frichti, as well as larger Fortune 500 clients such as Toyota.”

“After two years, I sold my shares and joined Bim, a food-tech startup. The company eventually shut down due to a lack of funding, which was a tough experience, but it reinforced something important for me: I wanted to be part of a company with both bold ambition and strong execution capacity.”

“In 2018, I joined Voodoo just as it was launching its apps division to expand beyond mobile gaming. That environment, fast, data-driven, and product-obsessed, was the perfect place to build what would become Wizz.”

items.t: Retail Holding to Absorb LabelVie in Major Moroccan Distribution Merger
sum: Marrakech – LabelVie and Retail Holding announced on Tuesday a merger that redrafts the competitive map of Morocco’s retail distribution sector. The deal will see Retail Holding absorb LabelVie through a fusion-absorption, creating a new multi-brand group listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange.
The boards of both companies met on Monday and approved the terms. A press conference was held on Tuesday in Casablanca to outline the details.
Under the deal, LabelVie’s equity has been valued at MAD 12.46 billion ($1.246 billion). The exchange ratio is set at eight Retail Holding shares for every eleven LabelVie shares.

The transaction is an all-share deal with no cash component. Once completed, LabelVie will be dissolved without liquidation. Its shareholders will automatically become shareholders of the new listed entity.
Retail Holding, currently LabelVie’s controlling shareholder, operates franchise brands in Morocco, including Kiabi, Burger King, Brands & Co, and Ansamble. It also runs King Cash in Côte d’Ivoire.

LabelVie is Morocco’s leading multi-format retailer, operating more than 411 stores across 37 cities under the Carrefour, Carrefour Market, Carrefour Express, Atacadão, and Supeco banners. The company employs over 10,300 people.

The merged group targets consolidated revenue of MAD 47 billion ($4.7 billion) by 2030. That represents more than a doubling from MAD 21.7 billion ($2.17 billion) recorded in 2025, translating to an average annual growth rate of 16.7%.

Cypriot SMEs to lead the way in digital construction shift
sum: Cyprus hosts EU workshop on BIM adoption for small construction firms

The Cyprus Scientific and Technical Chamber (Etek) recently hosted a European workshop titled “Scaling BIM Down: Making BIM work for small firms and small projects”, as part of its efforts to represent the country in the EU BIM Task Group and promote the adoption of the BIM methodology.
Building Information Modelling (BIM) is a collaborative, technology-driven process for creating and managing digital, data-rich 3D models of construction projects throughout their entire lifecycle.
The workshop focused on promoting BIM adoption among small firms and was organised within the broader goal of advancing the digital transformation of the construction sector.

According to an announcement by Etek, representatives from seven countries participated in the workshop, which took place in the presence of the two co-chairs of the EU BIM Task Group steering committee.
The event was held at a time when small and medium-sized enterprises represent a significant share of the construction and infrastructure market in Cyprus as well as across the European Union.

The main objective of the workshop was to encourage open dialogue and exchange of views on BIM implementation, allowing participants to share experiences and proposals on how SMEs can integrate the methodology and adapt effectively to the ongoing digital transition in the construction industry.

items.t: Women in BIM: driving global change through structured mentorship
sum: To mark International Women’s Day on Sunday (8 March), Women in BIM global vice-chair Marie Grieve offers five top tips for a successful mentorship.

The Women in BIM Mentor Scheme has established itself as a flagship professional development initiative within the global digital construction community. Designed to support women working across BIM and the wider architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector, the scheme provides structured, one-to-one mentoring that fosters career progression, leadership capability and industry confidence.

Founded as part of Women in BIM’s (WIB) broader mission to promote diversity, inclusion and equity in digital construction, the Mentor Scheme responds directly to a persistent industry challenge: the underrepresentation of women in senior technical and leadership roles.

While BIM continues to reshape the built environment, gender imbalance within the industry remains evident. The WIB Mentor Scheme addresses this disparity through practical, measurable action, equipping participants with guidance, networks and advocacy that support long-term advancement.

At its core, the scheme pairs experienced industry professionals with mentees seeking guidance at various stages of their careers. Typically structured over a six- to nine-month period, it follows a defined framework that includes goal-setting, progress tracking and regular structured dialogue. This formalised approach distinguishes it from informal mentoring relationships by ensuring accountability, consistency and tangible outcomes.
A defining strength of the programme lies in its international reach. Operating across multiple regions, it connects professionals from diverse geographic, cultural and technical backgrounds.

This global dimension reflects the collaborative nature of digital construction, where projects and teams frequently span borders. Participants benefit not only from career guidance, but also from exposure to various standards, workflows and leadership approaches.

items.t: This new Kensington Market spot for Bajan food has Drake’s stamp of approval
sum: From pop-ups to the Harbourfront Centre and now Kensington Market, Bim Street Eats has been spreading the soul of Bajan food across Toronto.

Focused on the flavours of Barbados, Bim Street Eats is the brainchild of chef Aiko Rudder-Jones, a young entrepreneur who moved to Toronto in 2013. While she initially planned to pursue soccer (or football, as she calls it), she soon found her true passion in sharing the authentic cuisine she grew up with.

“When I moved here there was no place I would really find food that I would get in Barbados,” she says. “I find a big way to have a piece of home is by eating food that you grew up with and that means a lot to you. That’s where the inspiration [for Bim Street Eats] came from — the fact there’s no Bajan restaurants in Toronto.”

Before launching Bim Street Eats while studying culinary management at George Brown College, Rudder-Jones says she was “lucky” to make connections that led to cooking at events for high-profile figures, including the President of Barbados, Michelle Obama and Drake.

When the pandemic hit in 2020, Rudder-Jones dove headfirst into the business, taking online orders, catering events and hosting pop-ups to share her love of Bajan street food. That momentum eventually led her to a summer-long run at Harbourfront Centre in 2025.

Now at 210 Augusta Avenue, Rudder-Jones’ soulful menu features classics like macaroni pie, BBQ pig tails, crispy fishcakes and fried breadfruit — a starchy tropical fruit and Caribbean staple. Plan your visit for a Saturday to catch pudding and souse, traditionally served on that day of the week.
“Pudding and souse is something you have in burritos every Saturday. It’s sold out by mid-day depending on where you go around the island,” explains Rudder-Jones. “It’s very, very, very popular.”

SGP IPO News - Chronic eye condition biotech SpyGlass Pharma sets terms for $150 million IPO
sum: SpyGlass Pharma, a Phase 3 biotech developing implants to treat chronic eye conditions, announced terms for its IPO on Thursday.The Aliso Viejo, CA-based company plans to raise $150 million by offering 9.4 million shares at a price range of $15 to $17. At the midpoint of the proposed range, SpyGlass Pharma would command a fully diluted market value of $549 million.SpyGlass Pharma is a late-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on chronic eye conditions by developing durable drug delivery solutions that provide long-term disease control and vision preservation. Its lead product candidate, the Bimatoprost Drug Pad-IOL System (BIM-IOL System), comprising novel, proprietary drug pads attached to an intraocular lens (IOL), is designed to be implanted during routine cataract surgery to reduce elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients who have either open-angle glaucoma (OAG) or ocular hypertension (OHT). The company is also developing a non-IOL-based, ring-shaped, sustained-release implant with bimatoprost, which it believes could be implanted in a standalone procedure, enable retreatment of patients who have received the BIM-IOL System, and offer extended care to patients with OAG or OHT who already received a prior cataract surgery.SpyGlass Pharma was founded in 2019 and plans to list on the Nasdaq under the symbol SGP. Jefferies, Leerink Partners, Citi, and Stifel are the joint bookrunners on the deal.

The BIM Trends That Will Define AEC Project Delivery in 2026
sum: The trends outlined below reflect how BIM is being applied today to meet those expectations, drawing on insights from Gustavo Gusmão, ENG’s BIM Solution Architect and Senior Developer.

While real-time collaboration accelerated rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic, Cloud-Based BIM has changed how project teams access and collaborate on 3D models. Most BIM models are still authored and edited using desktop applications; however, cloud platforms now play a central role in sharing, coordinating, and managing BIM models across project teams. Today, teams in different locations can coordinate around the same 3D model through shared access to published and updated versions. In most cases, BIM software is still installed and run locally, but the cloud supports:
- shared access to published 3D models across offices and regions

Increasingly, the cloud is also enabling multiple tools and digital agents to interact with the same coordinated model data. When a BIM model is hosted in a centralized cloud environment, published and federated model information can be connected to validation tools, calculation engines, and AI-driven services that operate alongside designers and coordinators.

Looking ahead, cloud adoption is expected to expand as browser-based and fully cloud-hosted BIM capabilities continue to mature, gradually reducing reliance on high-performance local hardware and supporting more flexible working methods. While cloud-based BIM improves accessibility and collaboration, shared access alone does not guarantee better coordination or construction outcomes. Ultimately, its value depends on how models are created, structured, and managed.

AI-assisted clash detection is emerging as a support layer for coordination teams, helping streamline the review process rather than replacing expert decision-making. Today, resolving clashes is largely a manual task: teams identify conflicts within the model and rely on experienced professionals to determine which trade should resolve them based on constructability rules, such as whether plumbing, mechanical, electrical, or structural elements can realistically be moved.

items.t: Designing with BIM and 3D: models, objects, and libraries for architecture and construction
sum: 15/01/2026 - Designing with BIM and 3D today requires digital tools that support the entire design process, from data management to spatial visualization.

The BIM methodology (Building Information Modeling) structures the project as an intelligent digital model. It includes three-dimensional geometry, technical, performance, and cost data, and enables multidisciplinary coordination, error reduction, and structured information management. 3D modeling, on the other hand, addresses the need to verify spatial proportions, test aesthetic choices, and communicate design intent to clients and collaborators through renderings and photorealistic visualizations.

BIM and 3D files are now among the most searched resources by design professionals. Finding reliable and usable content remains a common challenge, often due to incomplete BIM families, 3D models that do not match the real product, and compatibility issues with BIM authoring software and design software.
Archiproducts addresses this need with a platform where verified BIM and 3D files can be downloaded and integrated directly into the design workflow.

BIM design is a collaborative workflow based on a shared digital model. Unlike traditional CAD-based design, where each discipline works on separate drawings, BIM creates a unified environment in which architects, engineers, and designers operate within the same information system.

In Italy, BIM adoption is mandatory for many public projects and has become a consolidated standard in the private sector, making accurate and interoperable digital design tools essential for working with BIM software.

Each element within a BIM project is a parametric object that combines 3D geometry with structured alphanumeric data. A window, for example, includes information such as thermal transmittance, materials, manufacturer, cost, classification codes, and acoustic performance. These data follow international standards such as ISO 19650 and can be queried and extracted for automated quantity takeoffs, energy analysis, and cost estimation.

items.t: Framework for leveraging BIM to mitigate disputes in construction projects in Saudi Arabia
sum: Disputes significantly hinder construction projects by affecting timelines, budgets, and stakeholder relations. Building Information Modeling (BIM) offers potential to address these challenges, yet a structured framework linking BIM functionalities to common dispute causes across the project lifecycle remains lacking. This study develops and validates such a framework through engagement with industry practitioners within the Saudi Arabian construction context, where BIM adoption is now mandatory for public-sector projects. Ten leading dispute causes, and their corresponding BIM functionalities were first identified through an extensive literature review. A structured questionnaire was then distributed to practitioners, yielding 87 valid responses, comprising 42 from contractors and 45 from consultants. The Significance Index, descriptive statistics, and Mann–Whitney U test were employed to assess practitioners’ perceptions of BIM’s effectiveness in mitigating specific dispute causes. Results highlight that improved visualization, enhanced collaboration and communication, and improved data management were consistently valued as cross-cutting BIM functionalities across dispute types and project phases. Design coordination and clash detection consistently ranked highest, underscoring their critical role in addressing change orders and design errors. The resulting framework guides owners and practitioners on where to prioritize BIM effort across the project lifecycle to proactively reduce disputes and strengthen project delivery outcomes.

Disputes are a persistent concern in construction, posing serious risks to project success. As construction projects grow in scale and complexity, the number and severity of disputes have intensified. Industry data show the average global dispute value was US$52.6 million in 2021 (highest single case: US$2 billion), while in the Middle East the average was US$90.4 million (). These high stakes underscore the need for more proactive dispute prevention and management strategies.
Disputes often stem from the industry’s fragmented structure, with owners, contractors, consultants, subcontractors, and regulators operating under differing objectives.

Jimmy Carl Castle, 74, of Bim, WV passed away Monday, January 12, 2026. He was born February 15, 1951 and was a son of the late Curtis and Ina Castle of Twilight, WV.

He was preceded in death by brothers; Bob Castle of Orlando, FL, Charles Castle of Cleveland, OH, and Roger Castle of Wharton, WV, sisters; Billie Jean Doyle of Cleveland, OH, Bonnie Adkins of Cleveland, OH, Jewell Bailey of Twilight, WV, and Sue Pridemore of Madison, WV

He is survived by his wife Susan of 54 years, whom he adored and cherished; daughters, Malena Castle Mooney of Bim, WV, Melissa Castle Myers and Ricky of Mooresville, NC, and Rachel Castle Harless and Brian of Barrett, WV; his brothers, Jesse Castle of Danville, WV and Gene Castle of Madison, WV; sisters, Betty Penix of Dayton, OH and Ann Brady of Elkins, WV; grandchildren, Curtis Mooney, Molly Myers, Madalynn Harless, Benjamin Harless, and a granddaughter who will be born March of 2026, baby girl Harless; and a great granddaughter to be born March of 2026, Ivy Mae Mooney. Also surviving Jimmy is a host of nieces, nephews, and friends. Jimmy held deep affection for all his nieces and nephews and considered Ricky Bailey and David Castle to be like brothers to him.

Jimmy attended Bim Freewill Baptist Church and loved Jesus. He was a member of the UMWA Local 1503. He was an avid outdoorsman. He loved everything about the outdoors including fishing, hunting, Molly Mooching, berry picking, and gardening. Jimmy prioritized, adored, and loved his family, especially his grandchildren. Jimmy loved taking his grandchildren hunting and also taking them fishing at Smith Mountain Lake. He was always cheering on his grandchildren at their sporting events. He loved baseball and softball growing up and in his adult years, he loved watching Westerns.

Jimmy always had an endless supply of Slim Jims, Oreos, Ice Cream, egg sandwiches, mountain candy and TV dinners, this was for his grandchildren. He loved RC and Moon Pies. Jimmy loved sharing a sweet snack with his wife and loved reading and studying the Bible with her.

AECOM acquires AI startup for $390 million
sum: AECOM has acquired Norwegian artificial intelligence startup Consigli in a deal reported to be worth $390 million. The acquisition, reported by Norwegian newspaper Dagens Næringsliv, comes after the two companies had collaborated on multiple projects.

Consigli labels itself as an “autonomous engineer” and an “AI agent for real estate development.” Founded in 2020, the startup uses AI in planning and engineering, claiming that “up to 80 percent of today’s engineering work can be automated, freeing human experts to focus on innovation, oversight, and creating real value.”

Among the tasks automated by Consigli are MPE engineering, space analysis, unit optimization, and tender documents. The firm can also deliver clash-free Stage 3 BIM models with drawings, system strategies, and full bills of quantities and claims to cut material use in designs by 20%.
Last month, Archinect spoke with AI-native artificial intelligence company Cedar on the growing adoption of AI across the architecture industry.
